text:
Rae (product): Heads-up: Northstar Labs is asking for a private-deploy plan that guarantees near-zero downtime upgrades and lets their NetOps fully control routing. They want a phased roadmap, acceptance tests, and a clear SLA by next Wednesday. Key asks: customer-managed route tables, IP stability (no tenant IP churn), and an automated rollback.
Morris (eng-runtime): We should split into two milestones: M1 = customer-managed peering + orchestrated DNS handoff + canary + traffic-split mirror. M2 = VIP handoff / floating IPs + installer changes to preserve tenant IPs. M1 estimate 3w, M2 6w.
Clara (field): Northstar's ops team will only sign off if packet loss < 15s and any cutover is reversible within 5 minutes. They prefer BGP-based VIP moves but will accept controlled DNS if we can show it in staging. KMS + audit logs mandatory.
Ivy (solutions): For M1 we can offer a "traffic-mirror then split" pattern: mirror traffic to new nodes, warm caches, then slowly increment traffic weight. That avoids a hard cut. We'll provide a test harness and a runbook. Small example: 
```
# start mirror
curl -X POST https://deploy.redwood/api/v1/mirror -d '{"tenant":"ns-canary","target":"new"}'
# shift weight to 20%
curl -X POST https://deploy.redwood/api/v1/split -d '{"tenant":"ns-canary","weight":20}'
```
Morris (eng-runtime): Implementation details: need a control-plane flow to coordinate mirror -> cache-warm -> health-check -> weight-ramp. We'll add feature flags: "preserve_ips": "off|soft|strict" and "vip_swap_mode": "bgp|dns|mirror-split". Note: strict preserve_ips requires installer and CNI changes (M2).
Rae (product): Proposal: ship M1 in Q3: managed peering, orchestrated mirror/split API, canary promotion API, runbook, KMS/audit logs, and an acceptance test suite. Defer strict IP-preserve (M2) to Q4. We will align SLA wording with legal/finance. Thoughts?
Clara (field): Northstar will accept M1 if we deliver: (1) NetOps runbook with exact verification steps, (2) a staging playbook they can run end-to-end, (3) a cost estimate for reserved capacity during ramp windows. I'll collect the SLA numbers.
Morris (eng-runtime): One dependency: installer must accept customer route tables and static VIP assignment. I'll open an RFC this sprint and prototype a minimal VIP flow. If BGP isn't possible for a given customer, fallback is managed peering + mirrored swap.
Ivy (solutions): I'll draft the runbook and build the harness that exercises mirror->split->rollback. Sample rollback cmd: 
```
# rollback to old nodes
curl -X POST https://deploy.redwood/api/v1/rollback -d '{"tenant":"ns-canary"}'
```
ops-bot: Runbook draft created: /docs/private-deploys/northstar-runbook.md. Owner: Ivy. Reviewers: Morris, Clara.
Rae (product): Action items: Ivy to drop runbook + harness by Tue, Morris to publish RFC and prototype flags by Thu, Clara to confirm SLA thresholds and cost constraints by Wed. We'll present M1 plan at Friday steering and mark M2 as conditional on telemetry from initial customers. :white_check_mark:
